advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the zero-residual REVIEW_BOT_PORT assertion with ticket AC3 (bare-name comment mentions are normal); scope the check to unsubstituted `${...}` forms rather than any occurrence of the name.
evidence: infra/runbooks/nginx-edge-render.md:51: `if grep -n REVIEW_BOT_PORT /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf; then echo "unexpected REVIEW_BOT_PORT text"; exit 1; else echo "REVIEW_BOT_PORT fully substituted"; fi`
infra/runbooks/nginx-edge-render.md:60: "The current template contains only the braced form, so a correct render leaves no REVIEW_BOT_PORT text behind."
Ticket 08be-a081-7442-4ba7 AC3: 'The expected unsubstituted=1 (the line-6 comment) is documented as normal, with the reason, so it is not mistaken for a partial render.'
advisory.finding: The new `if grep -n REVIEW_BOT_PORT ...; then ... exit 1` check and its prose assert that a correct render leaves ZERO residual `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` text, coupling verification to the exact current template. This contradicts ticket 08be-a081-7442-4ba7 AC3, which requires documenting that ONE unsubstituted bare-name mention (a template comment with no `${}`) is NORMAL. If the template regains such a comment, the check produces a false `exit 1`.
scenarios: A future template edit reintroduces a bare `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` comment (as the ticket says the template historically had), causing this hard `exit 1` on a correct render
advisory.suggested_fix: Grep specifically for the unsubstituted template form (e.g. `grep -n '\${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}'`) so a legitimate bare-name comment mention does not trip the failure path, and document the AC3 rationale.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the loopback count check not depend on REVIEW_BOT_PORT being exported in a prior block (grep for the literal rendered port, or re-export/echo it in the verify block).
evidence: infra/runbooks/nginx-edge-render.md:31: `export REVIEW_BOT_PORT` sits in the earlier render code block, not the verify block
Template has 127.0.0.1:8080 (line 184/194) and 127.0.0.1:8090 (line 90/100) in addition to the two review-bot lines (67,77); an empty ${REVIEW_BOT_PORT} makes `127.0.0.1:` match all of them
blocking.finding: The loopback verification `grep -c "127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}"` depends on REVIEW_BOT_PORT being exported, but the `export REVIEW_BOT_PORT` is in a separate fenced code block (the render block). An operator running the 'Verify it took' block in a fresh SSM session has the variable unset, so the pattern collapses to `127.0.0.1:` and over-matches the Gerrit (8080) and op-cert (8090) proxy_pass/proxy_redirect lines, returning ~6 instead of the expected 2 — a false failure.
scenarios: Operator opens a fresh SSM shell to run only the verification block, or the earlier export scrolled out of the session
blocking.suggested_fix: Either re-`export REVIEW_BOT_PORT` (or set it) at the top of the verify block, or grep for the concrete rendered port value rather than interpolating the variable.
